biography.plain_text: Monrad Charles Wallgren was an American public official who served in both houses of Congress before becoming governor of Washington. An optometrist and jeweller from Everett, he brought a small-business background to public life. His later federal service included chairing the Federal Power Commission before retiring to private business in California.

long_biography.plain_text:
Olympic National Park was one of Monrad Wallgren's lasting contributions as a legislator. He repeatedly introduced proposals to establish the park, with early bills encountering opposition over the use of its forests. After President Franklin Roosevelt visited the peninsula, Congress passed the legislation, protecting a large area of mountains, forests and river valleys.

Away from office, Wallgren was a competitive billiards player. He practised at Everett's Elks Club, where mill workers and wealthier residents shared the tables. A three-day match there brought him the National Amateur Balkline Billiards Championship. The sport remained part of his social life alongside golf and local civic organisations.
